purpose: Cladribine is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), including relapsing-remitting MS, in adults. It is also used to treat a type of blood cancer called hairy cell leukemia. For MS, it helps reduce the number of relapses and slows down how fast the disease gets worse.
how_it_works: Cladribine works by targeting and reducing certain white blood cells called lymphocytes, which are the ones mistakenly attacking your nervous system in MS. Think of it like pressing a reset button on the overactive immune cells causing damage. By lowering the number of these problem cells, your immune system becomes less likely to attack your brain and spinal cord.
common_side_effects: Upper respiratory infections (like colds), headache, nausea, low white blood cell counts (which can make you more prone to infections), fatigue, rash, hair thinning, and joint pain. Your blood counts will be monitored closely during treatment.
warnings: Cladribine can seriously lower your immune system, making it harder to fight infections — including serious ones like tuberculosis, hepatitis B, and shingles. It should NOT be used during pregnancy or while breastfeeding, as it can harm an unborn baby. Women and men must use reliable birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after. It may also increase the risk of certain cancers. You will need regular blood tests and cancer screenings. Make sure your doctor knows all medications you take.
typical_dosing: For MS (Mavenclad tablets): Treatment is given in two short yearly cycles over two years. Each cycle involves taking tablets once a day for a few days, spread over two weeks, then stopping. Most patients take a low dose based on their body weight. After completing both yearly cycles, no further treatment is usually needed for at least two years. Your doctor will calculate the exact dose for you.
